Committee on Inland Fisheries & Wildlife  Legislative Information Office 100 State House Station Augusta, ME 04333
January 27, 2025
RE: LD 95, An Act to Amend and Simplify Certain Wildlife Laws
Dear Sen. Baldacci, Rep. Roberts, and Members of the IFW Committee:
My name is Francesca "Ches" Gundrum and I am Maine Audubon's Director of Advocacy. Maine Audubon is a wildlife conservation non-profit - we fulfill our mission to "conserve Maine's wildlife and wildlife habitat" by engaging people of all ages in nature through a science-based approach to education, conservation, and advocacy. On behalf of Maine Audubon and our 30,000 members, supporters, and volunteers, thank you for the opportunity to submit testimony in support of LD 95, An Act to Amend and Simplify Certain Wildlife Laws.
Maine Audubon supports the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlfie's (DIFW) suggested changes to Chapter 925, Subchapter 3, �12804, Conservation of endangered species. We concur with both the minor, clarifying updates to the language and including "species of special concern" (SSC) locations on the Freedom of Access Act records exemption list.
A species of special concern is any species of fish or wildlife that does not meet the criteria of an endangered or threatened species but is particularly vulnerable, and could easily become, an endangered, threatened, or extirpated species due to restricted distribution, low or declining numbers, specialized habitat needs or limits, or other factors. With recent adjustments in the list this fall, there are currently more than hundred SSC.
In order to allow DIFW and conservation partners the ability to adequately address conservation needs of vulnerable species, affording these species the same protections as endangered and threatened species is critical. Protecting the location information of SSC is important to their conservation because revealing their whereabouts could lead to increased poaching, habitat destruction, and other human disturbances, raising the risk of additional population decline. We strongly encourage the Committee to support this bill. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Francesca "Ches" Gundrum Director of Advocacy

February 1, 2025
Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife c/o Legislative Information Office 100 State House Station Augusta, ME 04333
Re: LD 95: An Act to Amend and Simplify Certain Wildlife Laws
Dear Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts, and Members of the Committee on Inland Fisheries and Wildlife:
I am John Simoneau, Maine Resident, submitting this testimony on behalf of New England Chapter of Backcountry Hunters & Anglers (BHA).
BHA seeks to ensure North America's outdoor heritage of hunting and fishing in a natural setting by supporting land conservation, public access to hunting and fishing areas, fair chase, and the sound management of fish and wildlife and their habitats.
On behalf of BHA's Maine members we are testifying in support of LD 95. Specifically, we are in favor of Sec. 12 MRSA 11401 that relates to the Department's rule-making authority to create special or expanded archery hunting seasons for the taking of deer to maintain deer populations in balance with available habitat. In recent legislative sessions there were adjustments to the any deer permit system in an effort to bring deer populations into balance. However, in some Wildlife Management Districts with any deer permits the harvest may still may not meet objectives. Increasingly residential development has fractured larger parcels reducing opportunities for the use of firearms. The expanded archery program was originally established to provide additional deer hunting opportunities in coastal and suburban settings characterized with high levels of residential development interspersed with small wood lots. It has a proven record of not impacting human safety and often expanded archery hunters are welcomed by landowners who are experiencing issues with damage to crops and landscape.
BHA supports making the two-day youth hunt permanent. We would suggest that the Committee and Department consider extending this opportunity to include novice hunters, which could be defined as a hunter who purchased first hunting or combination license within one year of the first day of this hunt. This is a hunt offered in Vermont, which could provide a more positive first experience for new adult hunters.
BHA also recognizes the value of non-game wildlife and supports the expanded authority to protect Species of Special Concern in Section 14 of the bill.
WWW.BACKCOUNTRYHUNTERS.ORG/NEW_ENGLAND_BHA MAINE@BACKCOUNTRYHUNTERS.ORG

In sum, we support the work the Department put into this Omnibus bill with only one suggested amendment for discussion. We would welcome more conversation with the Department around the concept of an Adult Novice hunt.

Sincerely

John Simoneau, New England Chapter Secretary Maine State Team Chair maine@backcountryhunters.org

10031442:
Maine Forest Products Council
The voice of Maine's forest economy
Testimony in Support of LD 95
"An Act to Amend and Simplify Certain Wildlife Laws"
Tuesday, January 27, 2025 Krysta West, Deputy Director
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. My name is Krysta West. I am from Readfield, and I am submitting testimony today on behalf of the Maine Forest Products Council in support of LD 95.
There are many different policy measures included in LD 95, but specifically, the Council supports the addition of "or species of special concern" to the confidential information provision included in section five of the bill. Under current law, the location of threatened or endangered species is confidential if the Commissioner deems that disclosure of that information would threaten efforts to preserve that species.
That confidentiality is important to the Department's recovery efforts, as the habitats that sustain these species are largely privately owned and managed. It also gives landowners the necessary assurances that supporting habitats for these declining species won't result in heightened public scrutiny and regulation. Keeping the location of these species on private lands confidential also reduces public use of private roads for "scavenger hunts" that can create high impact areas for sensitive species and increase road maintenance costs for private landowners, so it makes sense that this same confidentiality should be extended to species that are of special concern.
Extending this confidentiality clause as suggested enables the Department to proactively work with landowners on conservation efforts to recover populations and hopefully avoid the need for listings all together.
We would like to thank the Department and Representative Cluchey for bringing this bill forward. Please vote `Ought to pass' on section five of LD 95. Thank you.

183010:
TESTIMONY OF THE
DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND
WILDLIFE
IN SUPPORT OF L.D.95
"AN ACT TO AMEND AND SIMPLIFY CERTAIN WILDLIFE LAWS"
SPONSORED BY: Representative CLUCHEY of Bowdoinham
DATE OF HEARING: Monday, January 27, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. l am Nate Webb, Wildlife Division Director at the
Department of inland Fisheries and Wildlife, speaking on behalf of the Department, in support of L.D. 95.
This bill repeals certain provisions of law related to special regulations regarding deer
hunting seasons that are now redundant due to that language being placed in
Department of lnland Fisheries and Wildlife rule. This bill also reorganizes certain laws regarding rulemaking related to open and closed seasons for deer hunting and clarifies the distinctions between the expanded archery season and a special hunting season and corrects cross-references. It also creates a Freedom of Access Act public records exemption by making location data regarding species of special concern confidential in statute, just as location data regarding threatened and endangered species are.
This is the Department's omnibus wildlife bill that seeks to clarify and better organize
several areas of Title 12 that relate to wildlife conservation. Last year, as part of a
broader effort to align the use of crossbows with bow and arrows during archery seasons, the Department conducted rulemaking to move special deer hunting
regulations into Rule Chapter 16 - Hunting. Removing these regulations from Title 12 will reduce the opportunity for conflict between statue and rule and ensure that the Department has the flexibility to adjust these seasons when required. As part of this
effort, we also found that the current statutory framework for the expanded archery
season is unclear. Therefore, this bill establishes the expanded archery season as a distinct season from the other special seasons that the Department occasionally implements on off-shore islands and in other unique circumstances.

Finally, this bill creates an exception from FOAA for location data of special concern
species, which are species that are not listed as threatened or endangered but have the
potential to become so in the future. Currently, the Department must provide location data for these species upon request, creating a significant risk of illegal collection for some species. Allowing the Department to withhold records for these species, when doing so is important for their conservation, will help reduce the potential that they may need to be listed as threatened or endangered in the future.
I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.
